saint-luis-rey-cuba--linea-clasica.description: Founded before the Second World War, Saint Luis Rey most likely takes its name from the town of San Luis in Vuelta Abajo, the zone that supplies its wrapper, binder and filler. The Regios, a 48 x 127 mm robusto, is the only regular size left. Known among smokers who like intensity, it smokes savoury and mineral, with wood, earth and leather and a nutty close.

thirds.notes: A savoury, distinctly mineral opening that settles into wood and earth.
The minerality grows to match the wood, and leather arrives with a faint metallic edge.
Wood takes the lead with nuts behind it, a light bitterness and a metallic hint at the finish.

sources.title: Cigars Lover – Saint Luis Rey Regios review

saint-luis-rey-cuba--edicion-regional.description: Habanos uses the Saint Luis Rey name for regional editions. Two recent ones share a 54 ring gauge: the Marquéz for Cuba and the Herfing for the Middle East, the latter from the 2017 programme, each limited to 7,500 boxes of ten. Reviewers find both medium-full, built on coffee, wood and roasted nuts; the Marquéz adds bright acidity and dark chocolate.
